newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to raise minimum wage May 1.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to raise minimum wage May 1.

text.p: Venezuela would raise its minimum wage on May 1 even if Congress had not yet approved the changes in the Labor Law that were meant to precede the salary hike, a government minister said.

With pressure for the promised wage rise increasing, even as congressional discussion of the Labor law reform looks to drag on, "It looks as though the government will have to grant the rise (ahead of time)," Labor Minister Maria Bernardoni told reporters.

The raise will take the form of a temporary bonus payment, to be fully converted into salary once Congress finally approves Labor Law reforms that come as part of a wider revamping of Venezuela's crumbling social security system and rigid labor markets, Bernardoni said.
Government officials have said the hike in the minimum wage will be to between 62,000 and 75,000 bolivars ($129-$157) per month from the current 53,000 bolivar level.
The rise is expected to add some five percentage points to year-end inflation, officially forecast at around 35 percent.
